paragraphs: Rabbi Shmuel. (An amora of the Jerusalem Talmud, a student of Rabbi Abbahu.) As in Sanhedrin, end of chapter 1, where he said, "I posed it as a difficulty before Rabbi Abbahu"; and in Avodah Zarah chapter 4, halakhah 1, he said, "I saw Rabbi Abbahu prostrating himself as was his manner"; he spoke in his name, as in [Yerushalmi Shabbat 1:6](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Shabbat.1.6.2)[^3]; [Yerushalmi Yevamot 16:5](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Yevamot.16.5.5).[^1]

And likewise he spoke in the name of Rabbi Ze'ira (Rabbi Zeira), as in Kilayim chapter 2, halakhah 6; Terumot, beginning of chapter 4; Eruvin chapter 9, halakhah 4; Yoma chapter 4, halakhah 6; Shevuot chapter 1, halakhah 3, halakhah 6.

And it is possible that what they said in Niddah 15a, "Rabbi Shmuel said in the name of Rabbi Yohanan," is this Rabbi Shmuel; but what we find in Pesachim 112b, "Rabbi Shmuel said regarding a black ox," should read "Shmuel said," as in Berakhot 33a; Dikdukei Soferim.[^2]
And we have already explained in the entry Shmuel that he too is sometimes called in the Yerushalmi by the name Rabbi Shmuel.

notes.text: רבע כארחיה means prostrating himself in his usual manner. Guggenheimer’s [Yerushalmi Avodah Zarah 4:1:5](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Avodah_Zarah.4.1.5) discusses normal and sideways prostration and contains Rabbi Shmuel’s report about Rabbi Abbahu.
The identification of the Niddah speaker is only a possibility. The proposed correction in Pesachim and the cross-reference to the entry Shmuel are Hyman’s.
Hyman prints Shabbat 1:3; the corresponding passage is 1:6 in the linked edition.
